title:
Trump Orders a DOJ Review.
Israel Faces Coalition Talks.
Japan Assesses Quake Damage.
subject: Trump Orders a DOJ Review. Israel Faces Coalition Talks.
preview_text: A directive without evidence, a difficult coalition process and Japan’s overnight earthquake.
description: Trump calls for a review of Democrats, Eisenkot begins coalition bargaining and Japan assesses earthquake damage, plus Poland’s investigation.
contents_extra: Gaza’s shelter emergency, Poland’s investigation, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Trump Orders a Review of Democrats Without Providing Evidence of a Crime
paragraphs: Trump said Saturday that he was directing the Justice Department to examine Democrats over alleged threats against Republicans. Reuters reports that he supplied no evidence for calling their actions criminal. Democrats have promised congressional hearings and investigations after winning control of both chambers, with the new Congress taking office in January.

The president also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, referring to her comments about accountability for administration officials. CNBC reports that Trump did not identify the alleged communications, senders or recipients. An earlier Justice Department inquiry examined Slotkin and other lawmakers over a video urging refusal of illegal orders. A grand jury declined to indict them.

stories.title: Israel’s Coalition Search Moves to Eisenkot, With No Majority Assured
paragraphs: Gadi Eisenkot has the first opportunity to assemble Israel’s next government after President Isaac Herzog selected him Saturday night. AP reports that neither his bloc nor Netanyahu’s won a majority. The former military chief faces negotiations with parties that disagree over prospective partners and the direction of a future government.

The first deadline gives him 28 days, with a possible extension of 14. ABC reports that Eisenkot will receive the formal offer Sunday. Support in consultations is not the same as a coalition deal. Netanyahu remains a potential negotiating partner, while Arab led parties could influence whether another arrangement can win parliamentary support.

stories.title: Flooded Gaza Tents Expose Gaps in Shelter and Storm Response
paragraphs: Families in Gaza tried to rescue bedding and reinforce tents after heavy rain flooded displacement camps Saturday. Reuters reports that civil defense officials received 1,500 distress calls. Local officials said shortages of fuel and working equipment limited their response. Many residents remain in temporary shelters after destruction of homes during the war.

Israel’s aid agency said it had stepped up sanitation preparations ahead of the storm. Reuters reports that COGAT described four additional vacuum trucks arriving that week. Hamas accused Israel of restricting shelter materials; the agency did not immediately address that allegation. Residents told Reuters they lacked tarpaulins and tents, while bedding was soaked.

stories.title: Japan Assesses Damage After an Overnight Earthquake in Shizuoka
paragraphs: An earthquake shook central Japan early Sunday, breaking store windows and injuring at least 22 people in reporting checked at 10:49 UTC. AP reports that Japan’s Meteorological Agency measured the quake at magnitude 5.7. It struck at 1:04 a.m. local time, with its center in Shizuoka Prefecture.

The agency warned that further strong quakes could follow over the coming week. AP reports shattered windows and scattered books in affected communities. The U.S. Geological Survey measured the quake at 5.5, a separate agency estimate. Bullet trains were running at reduced speed as a precaution while authorities assessed the effects.

deep_dive.title: What Poland’s Investigators Are Examining After the Krakow Shooting
paragraphs: What happened. A gunman opened fire in Krakow’s Main Square Saturday, killing six people before police shot and detained him. AP reports that national mourning began Sunday and the square remained partly closed. Police also found three bodies at the suspect’s family home elsewhere in Poland. The investigation covers both locations.

Why it matters. The attack struck a busy tourist destination in a country where mass shootings are uncommon. Reuters reports that police and national security agencies are investigating. Officers who confronted the suspect were wounded and remain hospitalized. Authorities praised their intervention, saying it prevented further deaths as people fled the square.

What each side says. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said evidence pointed to an influence from extreme nationalist ideology. AP reports his description of the suspect’s radical views. These are officials’ assessments during an active investigation, not a completed judicial finding. Police confirmed the suspect’s age as 24 after conflicting initial reports.

What comes next. Investigators must establish the sequence of events, the weapons used and the relationship between the two crime scenes. Reuters reports that officers found weapons and ammunition in the suspect’s vehicle. AP reports that police identified the bodies at his home as his parents and sister. National mourning continues Monday.

photo.alt: St Mary Basilica towers in Krakow; file photo.

trivia.question: Which Japanese prefecture was the center of Sunday’s earthquake?
trivia.explanation: C. Shizuoka. AP reports that the earthquake’s center was in Shizuoka Prefecture.

poll.question: Should presidential requests for criminal investigations require a public explanation of the evidence?

World view: Syria disputes a Yemen deployment. A diplomatic source denied plans to send troops while describing closer military cooperation with Saudi Arabia; Reuters reports.
Hong Kong lawmakers reject criticism. The legislature condemned foreign governments’ objections to Joshua Wong’s additional 10 year sentence; Reuters reports.
Guatemala mourns four attack victims. A lawmaker and three police officers died in an armed attack in Zacapa, the president said; Reuters reports.
Malaysia’s king defends a decree. He warned against challenging his order allowing former Prime Minister Najib Razak to move to house arrest; Reuters reports.
Need to know: Delhi faces severe pollution. Authorities ordered schools to offer online classes and encouraged working from home ahead of Diwali; Reuters reports.
Tajani says hackers exposed his data. Italy’s foreign minister blamed hackers he described as sympathetic to Russia; Reuters reports.
Arthritis trial shows improvement. Johnson & Johnson said its pill improved joint symptoms more often than placebo after 16 weeks; Reuters reports.
Heart drug results disappoint. Novartis’ pelacarsen lowered a targeted blood particle without reducing major cardiovascular outcomes in a large trial; Reuters reports.
Money & markets: Google buys a development site. The Wyoming campus acquisition follows a planned $17 billion investment; the purchase price was not disclosed; Reuters reports.
Egypt and Libya discuss energy projects. Talks covered gas pipelines, refining and electricity connections, with technical discussions expected to continue; Reuters reports.
Melenchon outlines an economic program. The French presidential hopeful proposed a stimulus led revival while renewing his call to leave NATO; Reuters reports.
Leo Pharma weighs an IPO delay. Berlingske reported a possible postponement until 2027; the drugmaker declined to comment to Reuters; Reuters reports.
Future frontiers: Microsoft reassesses rented AI capacity. Bloomberg reported a winding down of Oracle computing arrangements; Oracle said demand for its infrastructure remained strong; Reuters reports.
Astronomers identify a double debris ring. A white dwarf’s unusual surroundings may preserve evidence of rocky bodies surviving stellar evolution; Reuters reports.
Landfill gas escapes collection systems. Satellite measurements detected major methane releases from Turkish waste sites ahead of COP31; Reuters reports.
Ukraine reports Russian satellite communications. Military intelligence told Reuters that Russia is using its Rassvet network over Ukraine; Reuters reports.
The score: Suns edge Rockets 102 to 99. Devin Booker’s late scoring helped Phoenix finish a game it had led by 19; Reuters reports.
Nuggets beat Pacers 114 to 102. Denver held off Indiana’s second half rally in Mexico City; Reuters reports.
Knicks defeat Cavaliers 109 to 97. Jalen Brunson recorded 31 points and nine assists in New York’s third consecutive victory; Reuters reports.
Hawks outlast Nets 124 to 121. Jalen Johnson scored 30 as Atlanta recovered from a 17 point deficit; Reuters reports.
Life & culture: Nandy presses entertainment companies. Britain’s culture minister said fear of career consequences still discourages women from reporting abuse; Reuters reports.
Tupac case attorney found dead. Police said Michael Sanft’s death did not appear suspicious; its cause remained undetermined; Reuters reports.
Gaza hosts a mass wedding. A ceremony brought together 250 couples, in a simpler celebration than many once held in the territory; AP reports.
Conservation groups weigh their AI use. Organizations use it to monitor wildlife and fires while acknowledging the environmental costs of data centers; Reuters reports.

uncertainties: CNN reports White declined, citing a source; one aide called the offer a joke, and White publicly said he would meet Trump Monday.
Japan’s initial injury count and Poland’s investigation remain developing.
Task Force Iron Gate is a new initiative, not proof that trade routes have been closed.
Eisenkot has an opportunity to negotiate, not a confirmed coalition.
